units: <cite ref="Mishnah Megillah 1:7">Meg. I, 7</cite>, a. e., v. <cite ref="Q01810"><he>פְּרִימָה</he></cite>.
M. Kat. 15ᵃ אין פ׳ אלא וכ׳ p’riʿah (Lev. XIII, 45) means, to let the hair grow (opp. to the opinion that parʿa means, to uncover, remove the headdress, v. infra).

senses.gloss: uncovering, removing the mourner’s wrap (v. עֲטִיפָה). Ib. 24ᵃ פְּרִיעַת הראש taking off the mourner’s wrap (on the Sabbath); Gen. R. s. 100.
uncovering the corona at circumcision, splitting the membrane and pulling it down.
units: <cite ref="Yevamot 71b:14">Yeb. 71ᵇ</cite> <he>לא ניתנה פְּרִיעַת מילה וכ׳</he> Abraham was not commanded to tear &c.

<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 6">Deut. R. s. 6</cite>, beg. (ref. to <he>למולות</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 4:26">Ex. IV, 26</cite>) <he>מכאן למילה ומכאן לפ׳</he> from this we derive circumcision and also uncovering.
<cite ref="Exodus 4:26">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <he>המול ימול</he> <cite ref="Genesis 17:13">Gen. XVII, 13</cite>) <he>שתי מילות מילה ופ׳</he> two operations, circumcision and uncovering; a. e.

<cite ref="Bava Batra 174a">B. Bath. 174ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>פריעת בעל חוב מצוה וכ׳</he> paying a creditor is a religious obligation, and minors (the debtor’s children) are not subject to religious obligations (therefore the guarantor who paid for them must wait until they are of age).
